hero.kicker: Spring and fall yard cleanups in West Bloomfield, MI
hero.title: Every leaf has to **go somewhere.**
hero.lede: A wooded West Bloomfield yard drops a mountain of leaves, and the wetland behind it is no place to put them. HD Landscape clears the beds and tidies the shrubs, and how the debris leaves goes on your estimate.

local.title: Oaks set the date. Water sets the limits.
local.intro: West Bloomfield cleanups come down to timing and where the debris ends up. Oaks hold their leaves late, low ground stays soft in spring, and township code draws a firm line between your yard and the wetland behind it.

points.title: Oaks let go last
points.body: Oak and hickory dominate what is left of the township's woods, and oaks often hang on to dead leaves long after the maples are bare. A wooded lot usually does better with a late fall visit, or two visits, so the beds do not fill right back up.

points.title: The wetland is not a leaf pile
points.body: Tipping leaves over the back edge is an old habit. Township code calls for a permit to put material in a wetland or watercourse, and it bars dumping yard waste on land you do not own. So none of it goes over the edge.

points.title: Compost needs room from the water
points.body: A compost pile generally has to sit at least 25 feet from a wetland, lake or pond, and it cannot sit on a drainage easement or swale. If yours has crept too close, tell us before the cleanup, because moving material near the water can need township approval.

points.title: Soft ground in spring
points.body: Capac soils hold a water table within a foot or two of the surface through winter and spring, and the low spots are slow to firm up. Heavy loads should stay off that ground, or the lawn comes out of a cleanup rutted.

points.title: The curb has its own rules
points.body: In season, the township's hauler takes yard clippings weekly, with brush bundled no longer than four feet and the rest in containers or marked paper bags. Stumps and roots are out. The definition of yard clippings even includes lake weeds, which tells you where you are.

logistics.title: Book a West Bloomfield cleanup around your oaks.
body: Spring visits start once the ground firms up, which can be before curbside pickup opens for the year. We clear winter debris, clean out the beds, tidy the shrubs and leave everything ready for fresh [mulch](/mulching/). Fall visits wait for the oaks when the calendar allows, because a cleanup done too early gets done twice.

On a lake lot, clippings and blown leaves should stay out of the setback strip and off the water. If you have invasive plants by the shore, tell us first, because removing them can call for township permits of their own.

faq.q: Do you do yard cleanups in West Bloomfield?
faq.a: Yes. HD Landscape does spring and fall yard cleanups in West Bloomfield, MI, from leaves and sticks to a full bed cleanout. We pull weeds, take out dead or tired plants and tidy what stays, and bigger jobs may add [weeding](/weeding/) or [plant removal](/plant-removal/) as their own lines on the estimate.

faq.q: When should I schedule a fall cleanup?
faq.a: Later than you might think if you have oaks, since they can hold their leaves well after the maples finish. On a heavily wooded West Bloomfield lot, a late visit or a pair of visits usually works better than one early one. Tell us what trees you have and we will suggest timing.

faq.q: Can I dump leaves in the wetland behind my house?
faq.a: No. West Bloomfield Township requires a use permit to deposit material in a wetland or watercourse, and the 25 foot setback around them is protected too. Township code does let a landscaper take yard clippings away for a residential customer, so your estimate can cover that instead.

faq.q: Will the township pick up my yard waste in West Bloomfield?
faq.a: Yes, curbside and weekly during the collection season, if it is set out correctly. For 2026 the township's hauler lists April 6 through December 11. Bundle brush no longer than four feet, with branches no thicker than two inches, and put the rest in containers or paper bags marked as yard clippings. Stumps and roots are not collected. Check current dates with the township.

faq.q: Can a cleanup include the area near the water?
faq.a: Up to a point. We clear lawn and beds near the water, but the township restricts removing vegetation or soil within 25 feet of a lake, pond or wetland. Natural growth there stays put unless you have approval, and we will talk through where that line falls on your lot.
